decisions.reason: Each utterance states sleep already begun, night or early hours (implied by “no escuro” at index 164), and waking caused by breathlessness: “acordar à noite com falta de ar”.

Each utterance reports difficulty or discomfort in breathing in the first person. Keying both homonymous entries with the specific positional term is the convention of the base Ortopneia and Trepopneia stories and of the batch's Flexopneia stories.
After waking, the patient improves on sitting and worsens on lying back; the letter of the description is met and nothing in the utterance contradicts it (B026-02).
Same positional wording, but the utterance also says “Adormeço sem incômodo” (B026-01).

No breathlessness on lying down and no relief on sitting is reported; five of the seven state that lying down or falling asleep was comfortable (160, 164, 167, 169) or that sleep had lasted hours (163), and 161 and 166 are silent on position.

findings.issue: Index 162 keys Dispnéia paroxística noturna, Ortopneia and both Dispneia entries. The utterance reads “Adormeço sem incômodo e acordo de madrugada com dificuldade para respirar. Quando me sento alivia; se volto a deitar, o ar fica curto outra vez.” The second sentence matches the wording of Ortopneia (“falta de ar ao deitar, que costuma melhorar ao sentar ou elevar o tronco”), but the first sentence says that lying down to sleep causes no discomfort; the breathlessness on lying appears only once the night episode has started, and sitting up for relief is part of that episode.

findings.issue: Indices 162, 165 and 168 give full credit to Ortopneia in addition to Dispnéia paroxística noturna because the patient, after waking, improves on sitting and worsens on lying back. Sitting up for relief is, however, also how a night episode of breathlessness usually behaves, so the two entries are not independent findings in these utterances.

findings.resolution: Passed. Both utterances state the upright position (“ficar em pé”; “Mesmo parado em pé”) and the improvement on lying down, which is what the source description asks. The script has no separate entry for exertional breathlessness other than the two Dispneia entries, which are keyed, so no un-keyed term gains support. Suggested polish: 173 make the relief immediate; 174 drop the comparison with walking.

findings.issue: The twenty story rationales are story-specific and each agrees with its utterance; the same sentence is reused as the evidence rationale of the specific term. The Dispneia evidence rationales (and the Ortopneia ones at 162, 165, 168) are a template with a missing full stop: “A fala documenta os critérios da entrada Dispneia: sensação subjetiva de diﬁculdade ou desconforto para respirar A hierarquia localiza o item sem comprovar etiologia.” The ten Dispnéia paroxística noturna stories share one alternativeAssessment.reason that mentions Ortopneia conditionally even in the seven stories where it is not keyed; the ten Platipneia stories share another. The rationale of index 179 mentions measured oxygenation (“sem atribuir alteração de oxigenação medida”), which the utterance does not raise.
findings.resolution: No rationale names an unrelated symptom, and no gender mismatch was found (index 167 “a paciente” agrees with “acordada”; 169 and 174 are masculine in the utterance and neutral in the rationale). No copy-paste leftover from another group. The rationale gap of index 162 is part of B026-01. Suggested polish: add the full stop to the template.

findings.issue: Index 161: “Não foi o barulho da rua que me acordou” and index 166: “Eu não estava levantando para ir ao banheiro” are denials aimed at the answer key rather than natural speech. Index 164: night is implied by “no escuro”, going to bed and the partner, not stated. Index 169: “o episódio” is clinical vocabulary. Index 172: comfort lying down is stated, not relief (“Posso ficar deitada respirando confortável”). Index 175: “Na poltrona” states the place; the sitting position is made clear only by “Se me sento de novo”. Index 177: the complaint is named only as “O problema” and repeats the source words “sentada ou em pé”. Index 179: “ereta” is formal and does not say whether sitting or standing.
findings.resolution: None of these opens another term or removes support from a keyed one. Suggested polish for a later edit: 164 say “de madrugada”; 177 name the breathing difficulty; 172 add that lying back down brings relief.
